title: Ablate R-017's page schedule: does the drifting chain still meet F-018 when its window does not follow the manuscript order?
statement: R-017 met F-018 (section vocabulary) with a line chain whose tables come from a window of 20 consecutive public pages that slides from the first page to the last as the synthetic book goes on. That schedule follows the manuscript's own order, so the generator writes each part of its book from the public pages of the matching section, and F-018 may pass because the section vocabularies are copied in by the schedule rather than produced by the procedure. Rebuild the R-016/R-017 procedure from its published method (every setting as stated there, fitted on public training pages only) and run three variants on the practice split, two seeds each: (a) as published; (b) the 40 window positions visited in a random order fixed by the seed, so the tables still drift but no longer track the book; (c) windows drawn from pages in a random order, so each window mixes sections. Report the F-018 statistic (context_mi by section, against shuffle_across_pages) and F-009, F-011 and F-016 for each, using the same layout as the fact attack. If (b) and (c) fail F-018 while (a) passes, file a second look on R-017 with assessment weak, saying that the attack imports the section structure through its fitting schedule; if (b) or (c) still pass, say so, and F-018 is met by any drifting table, which is the stronger refutation.
check: A source.json second look on R-017 ({"of": "R-017", "assessment": "weak" | "agree", "statement": ...}) carrying the practice values of the three variants; or, if the ablated text should be put on the record, an attack.json fact attack on F-018 with the variant that does not follow the manuscript order.
